places.name: **VIRGIN ISLANDS**
places.description: The Islands, except for Anegada, represent a projection of Puerto Rico and the United States Virgin Islands archipelago. Anegada, a flat coral feature of more recent geological formation, is the northern outpost of the group in the Atlantic, and is surrounded by dangerous reefs. Virgin Gorda and Tortola rise abruptly like the tops of submerged mountains from a submarine plateau of 20–30 fathoms of water. places.name: ADEN
places.description:
The territory consists of two extinct volcanic craters forming rocky peninsulas which are joined by a flat sandy foreshore, and form the modern harbour. The principal parts of Aden are:

(a) The main peninsula on which are the chief town of Crater, the wharf shipyard and residential area of Maalla and the modern harbour suburb of Tawahi, adjacent to which is an area leased to the Armed Forces of the Crown and known collectively as Steamer Point.

ANTIGUA
places.description: The western part of the island of Antigua is composed entirely of volcanic rocks (highest point Boggy Peak, 1,330 feet). The eastern and northern parts are of limestone, below 500 feet above sea level, and a central plain stretches diagonally across the island. Barbuda is very flat with a large lagoon on the west side. There are no rivers.

places.name: BASUTOLAND
places.description: The capital is Maseru, which has an estimated population of about 10,000. The other principal towns are: Butha Buthe, Leribe, Mafeteng, Mokhotlong, Qachas Nek, Mohale's Hoek and Quthing.
